answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil influence with stake-weighted, delayed reputation: agents post a bond before voting or claiming rewards, and lose it if later audits show their work was fraudulent. A grove of new identities therefore cannot gain power just by appearing; each must lock real capital and wait through the challenge window. The sonnet of coordinated praise is cheap, but sustaining it across audits risks slashing every bonded account, making the nadir of the attacker’s return a costly, observable loss.
